result.title: The Price of Precision: A Calibrated Cost Model for Mixed-Precision LLM Serving
result.summary: Choosing a mixed-precision configuration for large language model (LLM) serving trades speed against accuracy. Allocators that use average bit-width or a memory budget as a speed proxy can miss changes in the resource that limits execution. We argue that served speed can be limited by compute, weight loading, or key-value (KV) cache access, depending on the phase, batch size, and context length. A byte-based proxy does not capture all of these costs, so fewer bits do not always mean faster serving. To address this gap, we build a cost model that accounts for the binding resource and use it in two ways. First, as a predictor: given a configuration and operating point, it estimates serving latency using constants calibrated for the model, GPU, and serving stack. We evaluate its accuracy across three hardware classes. Second, as an allocator: we combine modeled time costs with measured per-tensor accuracy costs and use a dynamic program to select a configuration under a latency or accuracy budget. We compare its configurations against byte-aware and sensitivity-only allocation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文为 LLM 混合精度推理服务构建了一个标定的代价模型：区分计算、权重加载与 KV cache 访问中真正限制速度的「约束资源」，用它预测服务延迟，并结合逐张量精度代价，通过动态规划在延迟或精度预算下选择配置。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按约束资源建模 + 动态规划在预算下分配」的思路可能可供核查：LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的收益成本也可能受不同瓶颈资源支配，而非单一代理量（如字节数或 token 数），可类比为在延迟预算下分配精度或计算。
